subject: ventures/janitorial-bid-calculator
professional: a senior commercial janitorial estimator / operations manager who workloads buildings by production rate (ISSA 612-style cleaning times) and prices recurring contracts; first checks: hours = sq ft / rate x frequency x 52/12, a loaded wage, overhead on direct cost, margin as a share of price, that one-time project work is kept off the recurring monthly, and that drive, supervision and non-productive time are paid somewhere.

evidence.correctness: Independent Python (/tmp/claude-0/audit-janitorial-bid-calculator/indep.py, run with python3 -I, no subject import) re-derives the production-rate bid from first principles (hours = sqft/rate x freq x 52/12; cost = (labor x wage(1+burden) + supplies + equipment) x (1+overhead); price = cost/(1-margin)). Matches the shipped code to the cent: flat-rate page pair (18/h, 25% burden, $0.03 supplies, $150 equipment, 12% OH, 15% margin) light $2,386.18, heavy $2,948.24, heavy walk-away $2,506.00, carried-over flat quote $119.82 under walk-away and $562.06 under target; 5x-vs-3x page (index defaults: 2.4 h/visit, 17/h, 28%, $0.005, $25, 15%, 20%) 52.0 h -> 31.2 h, $1,720.00 -> $1,069.37, linear 60% $1,032.00; at $800 equipment $2,834.06 / $2,183.44 / $1,700.44 vs walk-away $1,746.75 (so 'under water' is right); second site 25 min x 3 trips: 10.83 drive h, $740.77. README claims recomputed: restroom 0.5 of 2.4 h = 20.8% of hours on 7.5% of floor ('about a fifth on 7%'), heavy/light labor ratio 1.313 ('differ by 30%'), 4 vs 52/12 understates by 7.69% ('about 8%'), $17 x 1.28 = $21.76 ('more like $22'). Fails: the 5x page printed $2,184 for 2,183.44; the second-site drive paid one person whatever the crew. Core right, one real logic gap off the main page: 3.
evidence.completeness: README features checked against code and tests: per-space rows with names and Other-space (calc.mjs:141, area-name.mjs), loaded labor, supplies/equipment/other, periodic services averaged into the month (calc.mjs:195), overhead on direct cost, margin-on-price, minimum price floor, capacity check, day-porter shifts with own wage, one-time projects and first-month invoice, copy/download bid summary, frequency cut with rebasing (calc.mjs:442), supply responsibility (553), initial clean (683), second site (second-site.mjs), share links and local save (share.mjs), proposal builder (proposal.mjs). All exercised by `node --test '*.test.mjs'` (242 pass before fixes). `node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs janitorial-bid-calculator`: no placeholder or retired origin in the served llms.txt/sitemap/robots/canonicals. Gaps: README usage-event list missed five events the pages record; proposal printing is not described in the README. 3.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/janitorial-bid-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 242/242 pass in ~0.4 s. quality_mutate.py, 8 seeded mutants in core logic: caught overhead excluding supplies (calc.mjs:213), one-way instead of round-trip drive (second-site.mjs:55), frequency rebase removed (calc.mjs:456), supply naive price without overhead (calc.mjs:595), initial-clean overhead on labor only (calc.mjs:709), capacity counting unscheduled areas (calc.mjs:263), periodic /13 (calc.mjs:207); survived: over-capacity > -> >= (calc.mjs:288). Page figures on the flat-rate page are pinned to calc output by a test; the 5x page's table was not (only $1,069 was), which is how $2,184 drifted. 7/8 caught: 3.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (804 lines), second-site.mjs, area-name.mjs, usage.mjs, the second-site.html script and index.html input wiring. Pure, well-commented ES modules with input validation that rejects zero production rates rather than defaulting. Defects: the money() formatter is copied five times (calc.mjs:343, 512, 634, 789; second-site.mjs:120) and number() is copied into second-site.mjs:15; dead branch `productionRate === 0 ? 0` (calc.mjs:234) after allowZero:false; compareFrequencyReduction labels rows with area.name instead of displayAreaName (calc.mjs:449); index.html is 1,691 lines of inline script. Acceptable to a senior reviewer with those nits: 3.
evidence.claims: Checked: every dollar figure on vs-a-flat-rate-per-square-foot.html (pinned by its test and recomputed), the 5x-vs-3x table (one figure off by $1), README 'fifth of labor on 7% of floor', '30%', '8%', '$17 -> $22' (all recomputed true), 'nothing uploaded' (no fetch/XHR in pages; usage.mjs writes localStorage only, honours DNT/GPC), production rates explicitly labelled ballpark not a standard (README, calc.mjs:22), disclaimer and no-SLA text on every page, CleanGuru page carries the non-affiliation clause and says its site was not reachable for live checking. Unbacked or stale: the README events list (5 events missing), the 5x $2,184. Source llms.txt uses github.io URLs but the served copy is rewritten (source-only, not filed). 3.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: a contractor bidding an 8,000 sq ft office at 5x enters four space rows, wage and burden, supplies, overhead and margin, gets $1,720/month, $0.215/sq ft, walk-away $1,376, a capacity check (2.4 h vs 4 h), can add a day porter, quarterly floor care and a strip-and-wax, copy a pasteable bid or print a proposal, and answer the three common renewal asks with tables and pasteable replies. A practitioner could submit a bid from it with their own rates. Gaps they would hit: no supervisor / inspection hours line, restrooms by sq ft not fixtures, no holiday weeks, no multi-year escalation, one building at a time with no client roster (stated: it is not CleanGuru). Usage is a local-only tally, so no reading ever reaches the repository. 3 with the stated limits.
evidence.domain: Compared with the workloading practice taught from ISSA 612 cleaning times and standard janitorial estimating (production rate per space type, loaded wage, overhead on cost, margin on price, periodic vs one-time work kept apart): the method matches, and the 52/12 conversion, margin-on-price and first-month invoice are exactly what an estimator checks. Departures: drive time paid for one person regardless of crew (now fixed); non-productive and supervision time only enterable indirectly; restroom workloading by area rather than fixture count; preset rates uncited (honestly labelled ballpark, and the ISSA 612 table itself is paid and was not consulted here, so the presets are not verified against it). 3.

defects.what: Second-site drive labor pays one person per trip whatever the crew size, and the page has no input for it: a two-person crew's paid drive time (and so the price that holds margin) is understated by half.
5x-vs-3x page table prints $2,184 for the 3-day $800-travel price; the calculator gives $2,183.44. Only the $1,069 cell was pinned by a test.
README 'Events counted' list omits five events the pages record (link_copied, proposal_printed, company_forgotten, periodic_service_added, periodic_service_removed).
Over-capacity boundary (> vs >=) unpinned: a seeded mutant survived.
No supervision / inspection / non-productive hours line; an estimator adds these to every workload and here they can only be smuggled in as a shift or Other cost.
Restrooms are workloaded by square feet only, not fixture count, which is how many estimators time them.
Monthly hours assume 52 working weeks: closed holidays are not subtracted and multi-year wage escalation is not modelled.
Production-rate presets are uncited (honestly labelled ballpark, but not traced to ISSA 612 or any published table).

money() copied five times and number() copied into second-site.mjs; dead `productionRate === 0` branch after allowZero:false; frequency comparison labels rows with area.name instead of displayAreaName.
Crew-capacity check sums every scheduled area into one visit, so on a mixed schedule (restrooms 5x, offices 2x) it checks the heaviest night, not each night.

verdict: A sound production-rate janitorial bid calculator: every dollar figure on its pages and every number claim in its README recomputes from first principles to the cent (one $1 rounding slip on the 5x page), the formula chain is the one a senior estimator uses, 242 tests catch 7 of 8 seeded mutants, and the renewal tools (5x to 3x, they-buy-the-paper, initial clean) answer real asks with pasteable replies. The worst defect was off the main page: the second-site calculator paid drive time for one person whatever the crew. Remaining gaps are scope (supervision hours, fixtures, holidays) and are listed in the README. Meets the bar at 3 across the board, not 4: it is a careful single-building worksheet, not the best available estimating tool.
